idiom_name: typed outbox module over node:fs (fsync + rename) or SQLite
implementation_notes: The Node primitives are the same as in JavaScript, but the durable contract belongs behind an interface so the store can change without touching callers: an Outbox<T> with append/claim/ack, implemented once over node:fs (temp write, FileHandle.sync, rename, delete-after-ack) and once over SQLite (better-sqlite3) when rows must be queried or committed with other state. Broker clients cover the hop, not the local store: a NATS JetStream stream with file storage and explicit acks (js.publish resolves on the server acknowledgement) or KafkaJS with acks: -1 and enableIdempotence covers the delivery leg, while the sender-side spool is still the application's to keep. Type the envelope (id, createdAt, payload, attempts) so the drain loop, deduplication and expiry rules share one definition.
pitfalls: A typed wrapper around an in-memory array is still not a store; the fsync or SQLite commit is what makes append() meaningful.
KafkaJS's idempotent producer is experimental and requires acks: -1 (its docs state this); otherwise retries duplicate records.
JSON round-tripping loses Buffer and Date types, so define the codec in the envelope or payloads silently change shape after a restart.
Floating promises in relay loops (a missing await on claim or ack) recreate the lost-message bug while still type-checking cleanly.
